newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Oil says sees 97/98 capex at 36 bln yen.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Oil says sees 97/98 capex at 36 bln yen.

text.p: Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd said on Thursday it expects to make capital investment of 36 billion yen in the current fiscal year, ending next March 31, compared with 38.6 billion yen last year.
The company also said it still considering merging its refining facilities with Showa Shell Sekiyu KK.
Yoshitaka Muto, Mitsubishi Oil managing director, told reporters: "We are still considering the possibility of merging (refinery facilities with Showa Shell Sekiyu)."
He said Mitsubishi was already cooperating in many areas of distribution with Showa Shell.
On the possible merger of refining facilities, there were still a lot of difficulties to be overcome but it was an important issue that needed to be addressed, he said.
Showa Shell Sekiyu KK, an oil refiner and distributor, is owned 50 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group.

In February, Mitsubishi Oil and Showa Shell said they were thinking of merging their distribution and refining divisions in a move that would help both firms cut costs. Such a merger would create Japan's largest refinery company.
The Japanese refining industry faces an uphill battle in trying to improve earnings a year after oil industry deregulation.
Muto said crude oil costs for Mitsubishi Oil in the last business year averaged $20.21 per barrel on an FOB basis. The figure represents an increase of $3.41 from 1995/96.
He said the yen weakened considerably in 1996/97, when the average exchange rate was 112.96 yen to the dollar, meaning the yen was weaker by 15.99 yen per dollar from the previous year.
Mitsubishi Oil's Muto said the company expected to pay an average $18.00 per barrel for the crude oil it purchases in the first half of the current fiscal year. The first half ends on September 30.
The average price of crude oil for the second half of the year to March 31, 1998 was forecast at $19.50 per barrel, he said.
